NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC FOR REGULAR MEETING
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection at the City Library.
Persons who wish to speak during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda, shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to the start of the City Council meeting. When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.
In compliance with Government Code Section 54957.5, copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the Agenda are on file in the Office of the City Clerk - 213 E. Foothill Blvd.; copies for public view are at the Azusa City Library - 729 N. Dalton Ave., Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.azusaca.gov. Persons who wish to speak in-person during the Public Participation portion of the Agenda or on a Public Hearing item shall fill out a card requesting to speak and shall submit it to the City Clerk prior to 7:30 P.M.; cards submitted after this time will not be accepted.
Those wishing to participate during Public Comment may do so in-person at the Azusa Auditorium, or may submit written public comments by emailing PublicComment@azusaca.gov. Emailed public comments are due by 5:30 p.m. and shall be limited to no more than 250 words. Written public comments will be provided to the City Council and will be part of the record but will not be read aloud.
View the City Council meeting live on the City?s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website.
Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations. Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code ? 21065.)? ?To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered ?projects? under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation.? If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a ?project? under CEQA.?

This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make public comments on items listed or not listed on this Agenda. Members of the audience will have the opportunity to address the City Council/Agency Board about public hearing items at the time the public hearing is held. Under the provisions of the Brown Act, the Council/Agency Board is prohibited from taking action on oral requests, but may refer the matter to staff or to a subsequent meeting. Each person or representative of a group shall be allowed to speak without interruption for up to five (5) continuous minutes, subject to compliance with applicable meeting rules. Questions to the speaker or responses to the speaker's questions or comments may be handled after the speaker has completed his/her comments. Public Participation will be limited to sixty (60) minutes.

Mayor Alvarez called the meeting to order at 7:30 P.M.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS:  ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS:  GONZALES

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Richman, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia, Chief
of Police Wenrick, Director of Administrative Services Johnson, Director of Economic & Community
Development Jimenez, Director of Public Works Delgadillo, Director of Community Resources Carpenter,
Director of I.T. Guadagnino, Deputy City Clerk II Hernandez, Planning Manager Vizcarra, Community
Improvement Manager Edson, City Librarian Hassen, Community Improvement Supervisor Hale.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Tommy Singh.

The Invocation was led by Pastor Felix Garcia, Centro Esperanza Church.

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Richman reported that five items were discussed during Closed Session, with no reportable
action.

CEREMONIAL

Presentation of a Proclamation Declaring February 2026 as African American History Month.

Councilmember Bow presented a proclamation declaring February 2026 as African American History Month.

Presentation of a Certificate of Recognition to the American Legion Post 180 in honor of its 100th Anniversary.

Councilmember Avila presented a certificate honoring the American Legion Canyon City Post #180 in
celebration of their 100th Anniversary.

Catalina Valera, representative of Congressman Gil Cisneros, also presented a certificate recognizing the Azusa
American Legion Post #180 and extended wishes for many more years of continued success.

Neya Upadhyaya, representative of Senator Susan Rubio, presented a certificate of appreciation to American
Legion Post #180.

Alexa Sanchez, representative of Assemblywoman Blanca Rubio, presented a certificate to American Legion
Post #180, congratulating them and extending best wishes for continued future success.

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
February 2, 2026
 Recognition of Community Improvement Supervisor Brent Hale for receiving the 2025 National Code Officer
of the Year award from the American Association of Code Enforcement.

Community Improvement Manager Edson presented a certificate to Brent Hale in recognition of his
achievement in receiving the 2025 National Code Officer of the Year award.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Kim Antol requested that the City Council consider hosting a Fourth of July celebration featuring food booths
and crafts.

Assistant Fire Chief Steve Cabrera reminded the community that the Fire Department issued annual defensible
space clearance notices on February 1st; noted that residents who received a notice and have questions may
attend the Referee Hearing scheduled for February 18th in Arcadia or visit the County of Los Angeles website
for additional information.

City Clerk Cornejo announced that the Big Banana Car is in town and will be offering rides to the community
over the weekend from 12:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez reported that he had no formal announcements but reiterated the Fire Chief’s
comments, adding that the City will also share information on social media and the City’s website to assist
residents who received notices.

City Clerk

City Clerk Cornejo requested the designation of a voting delegate and alternate for the Southern California
Association of Governments (SCAG). By Council consensus, Councilmember Bow was appointed as the voting
delegate.

Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Avila announced the 20th Annual Casino Night scheduled for February 13; announced the
American Legion, Canyon City Post #180 100-Year Celebration taking place on February 21 at 2:00 p.m.;
shared that the Azusa Boxing Program winter session will run Monday through Friday from February 2 to
February 27; informed the community of free seminars at the North Recreation Center, including “Home Safety
Presentation” by Visiting Angels on February 4 and “What is Elder Abuse” hosted by the YWCA on February
5; and also announced the Senior Valentine’s Day Dance scheduled for February 13.

Councilmember Mendez announced Tai Chi classes for seniors to be held on February 5th, 12th, 19th, and 26th
at the North Recreation Center; shared upcoming library events, including “Family Craft Hour” on February
10th, “Toddler Valentine Bash” on February 12th, and the “Family Brick Bash Building Club” on February
18th; requested Council consensus to bring forward, at a future meeting, discussion regarding a proposed $0.50
tax increase by the Board of Supervisors; and expressed concern regarding the lack of turnstiles at the Metro
Gold Line stations in the City of Azusa, noting that other cities have implemented them to address fare
enforcement issues, and suggesting that Metro be contacted to explore potential solutions.

Councilmember Bow announced that the Azusa Library will be hosting a Family Craft Hour featuring a
Chinese calligraphy workshop on February 3; mentioned that the Azusa Youth and Family Services
Department will be hosting a variety of social events throughout the month of February; reported the 3rd
Annual Lunar New Year event scheduled for February 28 at Memorial Park; stated the Azusa Renaissance
Community Theater students will be performing an adaptation of The Giving Tree on April 24; and shared that
she attended the Azusa Police Foundation Gala, thanking the board for organizing a meaningful celebration.

Mayor Alvarez announced upcoming classes, including “Hecho A Mano” art classes on February 4, Lunar New
Year crafts on February 17, and Family Story Time with Mulan on February 17, all to be held at the Azusa
Library; also reported attending the League of California Cities Conference in January; and mentioned updates
to Metro station turnstiles along with a noted fare increase.

PUBLIC HEARING – CONSIDERATION OF ADOPTION OF UPDATED CITYWIDE SCHEDULE OF
FEES AND CHARGES

Director of Administrative Services Johnson introduced Item D-1 regarding the annual review of the Citywide
Fees and Charges Schedule and noted that the purpose of the fees is to ensure cost recovery.

Budget and Revenue Administrator Lam provided a background analysis and explained that the proposed fee
adjustments are intended to account for inflationary cost increases; reviewed Staff recommendations, which
included incorporating previously approved development impact fees into the Citywide Schedule of Fees and
Charges without modification.

Staff requested that the City Council authorize annual updates to the schedule based on the percentage change
in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for the Los Angeles area, as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and
adopt the updated Citywide Schedule of Fees and Charges.

Mayor Alvarez opened the Public Hearing.

City Clerk Cornejo certified the publication of the Public Hearing in the San Gabriel Valley Tribune on January
22, 2026. There being no one wishing to address the council on this issue, Mayor Alvarez asked for a motion to
close the public hearing.

Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Avila, seconded by Councilmember Mendez and carried unanimously by the
following roll call vote of the Council to close the Public Hearing,

AYES: ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
NOES: NONE
ABSENT: GONZALES
ABSTAIN: NONE

Moved by Councilmember Bow and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Avila and carried by unanimous vote of the
Council to: Adopt Resolution No. 2026-C09, regarding various municipal activities and services, to be effective
on February 2, 2026; and Adopt Resolution No. 2026-C10, regarding development project services fees, to be
effective 60 days from February 2, 2026 (April 3, 2026).

AYES: ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
NOES: NONE

CONSIDER FIRST AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT WITH G2K CONSTRUCTION  FOR
MODERNIZATION OF SENIOR CENTER LOCATED AT 740 N. DALTON AVENUE

Director of Community Resources Carpenter introduced Item D-2 and provided an update on the Senior Center
Modernization Project; requested that the City Council consider approval of a First Amendment with G2K
Construction to complete the project.

Carpenter noted that initial project funding allowed construction to begin; however, once work commenced,
additional issues were discovered, including deteriorated sewer and plumbing systems, mold conditions, and
required code upgrades; she presented a new front entry design concept and reviewed project cost impacts.

Staff discussed the importance of implementing the proposed improvements and efficiencies to prevent future
disruptions and ensure long-term functionality of the facility.

The proposed expanded project scope would require additional funding in the amount of $1.7 million to be
added to the agreement with G2K Construction in order to complete construction.

City Council Minutes  Page | 4
February 2, 2026
 Councilmembers expressed concern regarding the increase in material costs and indicated a desire to revisit
Capital Improvement Projects to better evaluate and understand overall project expenses; acknowledged the
need for additional funding to address unforeseen damages; and emphasized that once completed, the facility
should be maximized for broader community use and additional programming opportunities.

The Council inquired about future plans to potentially connect the Library facility and the Senior Center to
enhance safety and accessibility.

City Manager Gonzalez shared a long-term vision of developing a cohesive civic center noting that City Hall
currently stands separate from the Senior Center and Police Department; stated that discussions have taken
place regarding connecting the three facilities, and that these conversations will continue following completion
of the current project.

In response to questions regarding funding, it was explained that approximately $4.5 million have been
allocated from the General Fund, with an additional $2 million coming from funds that directly impact
